title: Introduce hourly sliding-window quotas for ephemeral burst meters (reserved-aware)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add an hourly sliding-window quota tier for ephemeral burst meters used by short-lived requests (e.g., webhooks, interactive sessions) that: 1) provides predictable sub-daily limits, 2) is aware of reserved capacity buckets, and 3) preserves billing and ledger correctness across region failover and DST transitions.
background: Current quota model supports tenant-level monthly/daily windows and rolling 24h epochs for some customers. Many web-app workloads produce bursty short-lived traffic patterns where per-minute throttles are too coarse and daily resets are too coarse. Customers with reserved capacity need ephemeral burst budgets that don't incorrectly double-count reserved vs hosted usage when requests are re-routed or retried. Recent support tickets indicate surprising throttles during controlled load tests and billing ledger noise after cross-region failovers.
proposal: Introduce a new 'hourly sliding' meter type implemented as a time-decayed accumulator over the last 60 minutes with minute-level resolution. The implementation must: 1) be idempotent for retries, 2) participate in reserved pool accounting (charged first against reserved pool where eligible), 3) emit events suitable for billing ledger reconciliation, and 4) support regional sticky routing with consistent bookkeeping on re-route/failover.
design_details: Data model: store per-tenant ephemeral-meter entries as a compact circular buffer of 60 minute buckets (integer token usage) plus a running total to avoid full-scan on check.
Atomicity: use a single compare-and-swap operation per check+consume to ensure idempotent consumes; broker will surface deterministic request fingerprints for retry dedup.

Reserved-aware flow: when consuming, attempt reservation debit from tenant's reserved bucket first (fast-path); if reserved insufficient, debit hourly ephemeral meter and then fall back to hosted metering depending on policy.

Cross-region: shard ephemeral-meter keys with deterministic tenant-region key and a short-lived consensus lease (30s) to prevent conflicting simultaneous decrements during failover; provide reconciliation job to repair briefly divergent state.

Billing events: emit a standardized usage-event (proto v2) for each consume that includes: meter_type, meter_id, request_fingerprint, charged_source (reserved|hosted|hybrid), timestamp, region, and token_count.

DST/leap-second: rely on monotonic timestamps (NTP-monotonic offset) for sliding windowing; all persisted buckets indexed by epoch-minute number computed from monotonic base to avoid duplicate bucket when clock shifts.

Backwards compatibility: expose the new meter type via API feature-flag; default behavior for existing meters unchanged until a tenant opts in or policy assigns ephemeral meters automatically for eligible routes.
Performance: microbenchmark target p95 consume latency <= 2ms additional overhead; memory budget per tenant <= 1.5KB for buffer structure for 99th percentile tenants.
implementation_todos: storage schema migration: add ephemeral_meter table with compact circular buffer columns
runtime: implement AtomicConsume RPC in quota service with reserved-aware fast-path
api: new meter registration endpoint + admin UI toggle in Console to opt tenants in
routing: add deterministic tenant-region keying and 30s lease acquisition in shard manager
billing: update pipeline to accept proto v2 usage-events and add reconciliation tags
telemetry: add new metrics and dashboards (consume_count, consume_latency_p95, reconciliation_errors)
e2e tests: simulated cross-region failover, retry idempotency, DST transition simulation
docs: runbook for reconciliation job and FAQ for customers about hourly burst behavior
acceptance_criteria: Feature flag can be enabled per-tenant and default-off globally
Consume path decrements reserved pool first when available (verified by unit tests)
Idempotent retry: duplicate request fingerprints within dedup window do not double-debit
Cross-region failover test shows <0.01% ledger divergence and reconciliation job corrects any drift
Billing pipeline records charged_source and invoices match expected debits in a sample tenant test
Latency and memory budgets met in the performance CI benchmarks
Runbook validated by SRE with staged rollout plan and revert path
rollout_plan: 1) Internal dogfood on staging with synthetic burst tests; 2) Opt-in alpha with 3 tenants at low traffic; 3) Expand to 10 tenants after 48h stable; 4) Gradual auto-assignment to eligible routes after privacy and billing reviews. Each step gated by reconciliation telemetry and SRE sign-off.
rollback_plan: Disable feature-flag, run reconciliation to replay events from hosted ledger to restore ephemeral_meter buckets, and refund any mischarged hosted tokens if reconciliation uncovers inconsistencies. Rolling rollback scripts included in staging deploy.
testing_plan: Unit tests for circular buffer edge cases (minute boundary, full buffer, underflow)
Integration tests for reserved-aware flows (reserved only, hybrid, hosted fallback)
Chaos test: kill primary region node during high-consume window and validate reconciliation job repairs state
Billing test: synthetic invoice comparison for 3 tenants across 7-day run
telemetry_and_observability: Dashboards: hourly-meter top consumers, cross-region reconciliation drift heatmap
migration_steps: 1. Deploy schema addition as nullable columns; mark feature-flag off
2. Run background job to seed ephemeral_meter entries for opted-in tenants from rolling 24h usage snapshots
3. Enable feature-flag for alpha tenants and verify emitted billing events
4. Gradually opt in more tenants and eventually flip default behavior for eligible routes
5. Deprecate any legacy rolling-24h-only codepath after 90 days and remove migration flags
notes: This design trades a small per-tenant memory footprint for much lower variance in short-window throttling. The reconciliation job is required but expected to run rarely if deterministic leases and idempotent consumes work as intended.
